chunks: And from him, from Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who has a female slave and has sexual relations with her; is it permissible for him to marry her daughter?
He said: 'No, she is as Allah said:
And your step-daughters who are in your care
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of his female slave if he has slept with her?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sexual intercourse with a female slave (Umm Walad) establishes a permanent marital prohibition (mahramiyyah) with her daughter, mirroring the rule for free women. This ruling is derived directly from the Quranic phrase 'your daughters-in-law who are in your households,' which Shia jurists interpret as encompassing daughters of concubines due to the shared household and lineage connection. The hadith underscores the principle that the bond of 'having' (through possession or marriage) creates the same prohibitions as formal marriage.
